sources: Local MCP production of a four-page original, including approved scenario and element recognition
User feedback on making people and their actions distinguishable in finished pages
Comparison of nine preceding one-page works with the local MCP manuscript

findings.observation: Shared costumes and a rear or obstructed view made the reader work to identify the actor or speaker.
findings.rule: Use visible distinguishing features for that panel and tie each cue to the correct action or speech; review at reading size.
findings.reason: This helps when cues determine story comprehension without adding a pose or uniform to every scene.

findings.observation: The release task also included user-specific publishing destinations, author and watermark preferences.
findings.rule: Keep these choices in local private preferences or in explicit work settings.
findings.reason: They are independent of the operation and default behavior of the distribution.
